The instant complaint has been filed U/s.200 of Cr.P.C., by the complainant alleging tha
t, the accused persons have committed the offence punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act (hereinafter referred to as "the Act").

2. The complainant's case in nutshell is as under:
That on 30.11.2022 while CW-1/PW-1 being the Food Safety Officer, having visited the shop premises of accused No.1, he being the Proprietor of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Rice Traders, No.3, Nagasettyhalli Main Road, Bengaluru was found to be selling the Basmati Rice, manufactured and supplied by accused No.2 being Proprietor and Managing Director of M/s. Work 3 located at Sonipal Nearala Road,
Dharmakanta Village, Sonipat District, Hariyana.

The aforesaid official suspecting the quality and label conditions of the Basmati Rice packets of 1 Kg, proceeded to collect four packets of Basmati Rice of 1 Kg each by preparing Form No.VA of the Act and by serving the copy of the aforesaid Form on the accused No.1 in the presence of one independent witness by drawing mahazar.

Thereafter, the PW-1 forwarded the aforesaid four samples of Basmati Rice packets by wrapping them in the thick brown paper by affixing the slip containing signature of the accused No.1 and Designated Officer attached to BBMP North Division, Bengaluru to the analysis by Food Analyst by intimating the accused No.1 regarding his right for independent examination at NABL Laboratory, which was refused by accused No.1.

The aforesaid one sample of Rice packet was handed over to the Food Analyst along with Form No.VI and Specimen Seal Form and remaining three samples were handed over to the Designated Officer attached to BBMP, North Division, Bengaluru.

3. The Food Analyst vide report dated 13.12.2022 declared the sample i.e., Basmati Rice of 1 Kg as "Not Confirming to the FSS Regulations, 2011 as Thiamethoxam Pesticide is beyond the limits"
thereby held the subject food as "Unsafe".
Hence, the instant complaint.
4. The accused persons appeared on service of summons through their counsel and were released on bail.

The copy of the complaint and other documents came to be furnished to them in compliance of Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
5.
The substance of the accusation was recorded by reading over and explaining its contents to the accused persons, they denied the same and claimed to be tried.

6. The complainant in order to bring home the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts, got examined three witnesses as PW's-1 to 3 and got marked in all 12 documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-7, Ex.P-7(a) to Ex.P-11 and got closed its side of evidence.
7. The statement of accused persons as contemplated U/s.313 of Cr.P.C., was recorded.
The accused persons denied the incriminating evidence in the testimonies of the PW's-1 to 3 on their behalf and have not chosen to adduce their defence evidence.

The counsel for the accused No.2 submitted the authority in support of his arguments.

10. Having due regard to the complaint, evidence on record and arguments addressed by the rival parties, the following points would arise for the consideration of this court namely:
1. Whether the complainant proves beyond all reasonable doubts that, the accused No.1 being the Retailer and accused No.2 being the Supplier and Manufacturer of Basmati Rice have been involved in manufacturing, selling and storing as well as distribution of mis-branded food i.e., Basmati Rice, which was found to be "Unsafe"
for Human Consumption on account of excess Thiamethoxam pesticide as per the Analysis Report dated 13.12.2022 and thereby committed offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the FSS Act, 2006?
2. What order?

11. The answer of this court to the aforesaid points is as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2 : As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS 12. Point No.1: In the case on hand, the complainant is bound to establish the fact of accused No.1 being the Retailer involved in the storing and selling of mis-branded food i.e., Basmati Rice being supplied and manufactured by accused No.2.
Thereby, the accused persons have committed the offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the FSS Act, 2006.
13. The Food Safety Officer by name Sri. G. Govindharaju arrayed as CW-1 in support of the allegations set out in the complaint, got examined himself as PW-1.

The said witness has accounted as to having conducted routine inspection in the shop premises of accused No.1 on 30.12.2022,
having collected four samples of Basmati Rice packets of 1 Kg each by obtaining receipt for Rs.405/-
by drawing the mahazar in the presence of accused No.1 and witness by name Nithin so also, having prepared Form No.VA.

He has also narrated regarding the sample being sent to Food Analyst along with Specimen Seal Form and Form No.VI as well as receipt of the report from Food Analyst regarding the subject sample being "Unsafe" for human consumption.
14. In support of the said testimony, the PW-1 has got marked in all seven documents as Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-7.
Ex.P-1 is the receipt dated 30.11.2022 bearing seal and signature of accused No.1.

Ex.P-2 is the mahazar dated 30.11.2022 claiming to be drawn by the PW-1 in the shop premises of accused Food Safety Officer vs Anil Kumar on 30 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/

Ex.P-7 is the Form under Rule 2.4.10(iii) of FSS Act, dated 30.11.2022, wherein, the accused No.1 has refused to exercise the right of examination of the four samples before the NABL Laboratory.
The said document bears the signature of one Mr. Nithin.

15. PW-1 has been subjected to cross-examination by the counsel for the accused No.2, wherein, it has been admitted regarding the PW-1 having not received any complaint from the public with respect to having undergone health issues on consuming the India Gate Basmati Rice.
The witness has accounted as to having not examined the other rice brands being sold by accused No.1 at his shop.

The witness has pleaded ignorance regarding Thiamethoxam pesticide being used in the rice packets to preserve the rice from being spoiled and the same could be removed by washing the rice before cooking.
It has been categorically admitted as to the PW-1 having not issued notice to distributor or manufacturer as required under Rule 2.4.1.4 of the FSSA Rules, 2011.
It is also admitted regarding the chances of duplicate branded rice packets being sold in the market by manipulating the brand name and brand packets.
It is also deposed as to having not seized invoices to show the samples in the case on hand being pertaining to Batch No.B7451, procured from accused No.2.
It is admitted as to there is no any reference in Ex.P-3 to Ex.P-5 regarding India Gate Basmati Rice.
It is also admitted as to there is no any reference with respect to the seized samples in the Ex.P-7.
The other suggestions as to the accused No.2 is not guilty of having committed the offences alleged in the complaint has been categorically denied by the witness.
16. The counsel for the accused No.1 has adopted the cross-examination conducted by accused No.2 with the permission of this court.
17. The CW-3 by name Mr. Nithin is examined as PW-2.

This witness has deposed as to around two years prior to the date on which, the witness has deposed before this court, while returning back home, he has affixed his signatures on blank papers near Grocery Shop situated at Nagashettyhalli,
Bengaluru, on the pretext of having conducted Swach Bharat Survey.
18.

The PW-2 was treated as hostile witness and permitted to be cross-examined by the learned Sr.
APP, but the endeavors on his part to elicit the complainant's case as per the Ex.P-2 & Ex.P-3 has turned futile exercise.
19. The complainant by name Sri. Srinivasalu A., in the case on hand, has been cited as CW-5 with permission of this court vide order dated 20.03.2024 and has been examined as PW-3.
This witness has accounted regarding the investigation being taken over by him as per the directions of the Designated Officer i.e., CW-4 to prosecute the accused persons in the case on hand.

He has deposed Food Safety Officer vs Anil Kumar on 30 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/

20. In support of the oral testimony of the PW-3, in all five documents are marked as Ex.P-7(a) to Ex.P-11.

Ex.P-7(a) is the letter dated 20.02.2023 addressed to Food Safety Commissioner,
Bengaluru seeking permission to prosecute the accused persons.

Ex.P-8 & Ex.P-9 are the letters dated 20.02.2023 addressed to accused Nos.1 & 2 intimating their right to challenge the report of Food Analyst within one month from the receipt of the said letters before the CFTRI, Mysore.
Ex.P-10 is the sanction order dated 18.04.2023 issued by Food Safety Commissioner, Bengaluru authorizing the witness to prosecute the accused persons in the case on hand.
Ex.P-11 is the complaint.

21. PW-3 has been subjected to the cross-examination by the counsel for the accused No.2, wherein,
the witness has categorically admitted as to himself not having personal knowledge and information regarding the incident in the case on hand having taken place at the shop premises of accused No.1.
The witness has pleaded ignorance regarding the report as per Ex.P-6 is not pertaining to the authorized laboratory.

22. PW-3 has been subjected cross-examination by the counsel for the accused No.1, wherein, he has admitted regarding having not submitted postal acknowledgment pertaining to the due service of Ex.P-8 on accused No.1.
The other suggestions as to the witness is deposing falsely at the instance of his superiors has been denied by the witness.

23. The accused persons have not chosen to adduce their evidence in support of their defence set out during the cross-examination of PW's-1 to 3.
24.

The learned Sr. APP for the complainant vehemently argued that, the accused persons having violated the provisions of FSS Act, 2006 and thereby committed offences punishable U/s.52 & 59 of the Act is very much forthcoming as per the testimonies of PW's-1 & 3.
It is also highlighted regarding the examination-in-chief of PW's-1 & 3 so also regarding the documents Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-11 in support of his arguments.
Amongst these arguments, it has been sought to convict the accused persons in the case on hand.

25. The learned counsel for the accused persons emphatically argued that, the instant complaint against accused persons is not tenable as the mense rea as required U/s.48 of the Act has not been demonstrated by the complainant.

It is also highlighted as to there is no any iota of evidence to incriminate the accused persons to show the accused persons had knowledge regarding the subject matter being "Unsafe for Human Consumption".

It is also envisaged as to there is violation of Rule 7A of Food Safety Rules, 2011, amended 2023, so also, pursuant to violation of Section 46(4) of the Act due to Ex.P-6 not being duly served upon accused Nos.1 & 2.
It is also emphasized as to Ex.P-3 to Ex.P-6 does not refer to India Gate Basmati Rice.

The cross-examination of PW's-1 & 3 has been highlighted by pointing out PW-2 having turned hostile and amongst these arguments, it is sought Food Safety Officer vs Anil Kumar on 30 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/
5 to acquit the accused persons.

sentences.text:
"Evaluation of Evidence as well as Claim and Contentions of either parties"
26.

On overall examination of evidence on record, arguments canvassed by the rival parties, this court as to determine as to whether the accused persons being retailer and supplier/manufacturer of the Rice in question respectively have intentionally and deliberately with a knowledge have been involved in selling and supplying/manufacturing the rice, which was found to be "Unsafe" for human consumption and thereby committed the offences alleged in the case on hand.
27. The factum of seizure of subject matter is a crucial aspect in order to incriminate the accused No.1.
The aspect of seizure of the subject matter from the shop premises of the accused No.1 in the presence of independent witness PW-2, is unable to be gathered by the testimony of the said PW-2.
The version of PW-2 is very much contrary to the complainant's case, so also, the documents on record i.e., Ex.P-2 & Ex.P-3.

The sole testimony of PW-1 i.e., the seizing official, in absence of corroboration by the independent witness PW-2 creates a doubt in the mind of the court regarding the very seizure of the subject matter from the shop premises of the accused No.1.
This aspect certainly inclines the court to give the benefit of doubt in favour of the accused persons.
28. It is significant to note that, Section 48 of the Act shall be duly considered while deciding the allegations of commission of the offences U/s.52 & 59 of the Act.

The plain reading of Section 48(1)
of the Act mandates the deliberate intention and knowledge on the part of the accused, which resulted in commission of offences needs to be analyzed by the court.

In the case on hand, there is no iota of evidence on record disclosing the intention on the part of the accused Nos.1 & 2 to sell and manufacture the subject matter, though they had knowledge as to the same being "Unsafe" for human consumption.

29. Further, the mandate of the Act as contemplated U/s.46(4) of the Act regarding the report of the Food Analyst could not be challenged before the Referral Food Laboratory as notified by the Authority, pursuant to

the report as per Ex.P-6 not being communicated by the complainant authority to the accused persons is certainly a valid defence, as there is no any iota of evidence on record to demonstrate the intimation regarding the Ex.P-6 being duly served on the accused persons.

30. The report as per Ex.P-6 as well as the Form No.VA, Form VI and acknowledgment i.e., Ex.P-3 to Ex.P-5 respectively not referring to the subject matter by its name i.e., India Gate Basmati Rice, is also the justifiable defence pursuant to the obligation on the part of the complainant to demonstrate the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.

The said defence of the accused persons will certainly be the valid ground pursuant to the accused No.1 disputing the very seizure of the subject matter, so also, in light of the accused No.2 disputing the very supply of the subject matter to the accused No.1.

It is also pertinent to note that, the aforesaid defence in view of failure on the part of the complainant to produce the necessary documents pertaining to the supply by accused No.2 to the accused No.1, the relevant documents pertaining to accused No.1 having paid for the supply of the subject matter in the back drop of PW-2 having turned hostile will be the Food Safety Officer vs Anil Kumar on 30 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23896643/
6

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: tenable defence.
The accused persons are also entitled to the benefit of doubt on this aspect.
31. This court is bound to consider the complainant's case having been established beyond all reasonable doubts.

In the light of the discussion made supra, an anxious examination of testimonies of PW's-1 & 3, certainly inclines the court to hold as to the complainant's case is tainted with substantial omissions, improvements and contradictions as well as substantial non-disclosure of material facts.

Hence, this court is justified to hold that, the complainant has miserably failed to bring home the mens-rea which is the pre- requisite in the criminal cases as laid down in the catena of decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court as well as our Hon'ble High Court so also U/s.48(1) of the Act.
In the light of discussion made supra, this court holds that the complainant has miserably failed to bring home the guilt of the accused persons beyond all reasonable doubts.
Accordingly, this court without any hesitation proceeds to answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
32. Point No.2:

In the light of the discussion and findings, assigned supra while appreciating the Point No.1, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
By exercising the power conferred under section 255(1) of Cr.P.C., the accused Nos.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted of the offence punishable under section 52 & 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act.
Consequently, the accused persons are set at liberty.
The bail bond of the accused Nos.1 & 2 stands canceled.

Consequently, the accused persons are set at liberty.
The bail bond of the accused Nos.1 & 2 stands canceled.

As the Judgment is one of imposition of the acquittal,
considering health condition of accused No.2, the IA stands allowed.
The absence of accused No.2 stands exempted.
